stem: Meera lives in Delhi and her cousin Ravi lives in Singapore, close to the Equator. Both note the length of daytime on 21 June. Which statement about their observations is correct?

options.text: Meera and Ravi both record about 12 hours of daytime, because day length is the same everywhere on a given day
Meera records her longest day of the year, while Ravi's day stays close to 12 hours
Ravi records his longest day of the year, while Meera's day stays close to 12 hours
Meera records her shortest day of the year, because June is winter in the Northern Hemisphere

teacher.key_rationale: Delhi is in the Northern Hemisphere, so around 21 June (summer solstice) it experiences its longest day; near the Equator, day length stays near 12 hours all year. Only B states both correctly. A is the trap for students who drop the latitude condition and assume equal day length everywhere; C swaps the two places; D reverses the season.
